title: New connection-pool reaper drains the whole pool before refilling any of it
diff: +        """Run periodically in a background thread: idle connections
+        that have sat unused past STALE_AFTER_S are pinged and, if
+        dead, replaced -- keeps the pool from accumulating connections
+        a firewall or DB restart has silently killed."""
+            if conn.idle_seconds() > STALE_AFTER_S and not conn.ping():
+- New background reaper for the DB connection pool: pings idle
+  connections older than STALE_AFTER_S every REAP_INTERVAL_S and
+  replaces any that fail to respond, so a firewall reset or DB
+  restart no longer leaves dead connections sitting in the pool.

ground_truth.explanation: reap_stale_connections first drains every connection out of the queue with a tight get_nowait() loop, and only afterward pings and puts each one back, one at a time. For the full duration of that drain-then-ping pass -- proportional to POOL_SIZE times a ping's network latency, not to how many connections are actually stale -- the pool is entirely empty from acquire()'s point of view, so any concurrent request can hit PoolExhausted even though no connection is actually leaked or unavailable, just temporarily held by the reaper. The bug is timing-dependent and correlates exactly with REAP_INTERVAL_S, which makes it easy to mistake for unrelated load spikes in production. The included test exercises reap correctness (does it replace a dead connection) but never exercises reap concurrently with acquire(), so it passes either way.\n\nOffline validation (execution_validated): a standalone reproduction ran the reaper in a background thread and probed acquire() with a short timeout while it ran, compared against a one-connection-at-a-time reap strategy. The drain-all approach produced spurious PoolExhausted failures in every one of 15 trials (mean 4/40 probes); the one-at-a-time approach produced zero in all 15 trials.
ground_truth.validation_note: Standalone threading simulation: reaper running in a background thread while concurrent acquire() probes (short timeout) run against it, drain-all-then-refill vs one-at-a-time reap, 15 trials of 40 probes each. Drain-all: 4/40 spurious PoolExhausted failures in every trial. One-at-a-time: 0/40 in every trial. Script and raw output preserved as private provenance, not in this repository.
